Yes — the closest matches are training-free graph retrieval methods that aim to find minimal, query-relevant evidence subgraphs from a knowledge graph. GFM-Retriever directly returns a subgraph using a pre-trained Graph Foundation Model and a label-free selector to find an informationally sufficient and structurally minimal “core set” [1]. BubbleRAG is also training-free and frames retrieval as finding an optimal informative subgraph over black-box knowledge graphs, while QAFD-RAG is training-free and dynamically adapts traversal to the query’s semantics with retrieval guarantees [5, 3].

If you specifically want “without needing to train the system,” [1], [3], and [5] fit best. [1] emphasizes a pre-trained model plus label-free selection; [5] focuses on evidence-driven retrieval over unknown-schema graphs; [3] emphasizes query-aware traversal with statistical guarantees.
